recipes.name: White Bean Chicken Chili
ingredients_raw: 1 (18.75 ounce) can tomatillos, drained and chopped
2 ears fresh corn, kernels cut from cob
1 pinch salt and black pepper to taste

steps.text: Heat oil in a large pot, and cook onion and garlic until soft.
Stir in broth, then add in tomatillos, tomatoes, and chiles. Stir together and season with oregano, coriander, and cumin. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 10 minutes.
Add chicken, beans, and corn; simmer 5 minutes. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

raw_recipe.headline: White Bean Chicken Chili
raw_recipe.description: This hearty white bean chicken chili is made with cooked chicken, simmered in a spicy stock with beans, tomatillos, green chilies, tomatoes, and corn.

review.reviewBody:
This is my favorite chili recipe not only because its incredibly delicious, but because its one of the healthiest entrees you can make.

I followed others' suggestions and added 2 tablespoons of cornstarch, 2 diced jalapenos (some said this was a little too hot, but I thought it just about right), canned corn instead of fresh, and salsa verde instead of canned tomatillos. One thing to remember is that the quality of the Salsa Verde (or tomatillos) is very important as it is perhaps the predominant flavor. Make sure to use a good quality salsa--that is, one you really enjoy on its own. I prefer Target's "Archer Farms Salsa Verde", which is about $3 for 24oz.

I would give this 6 stars if I could! A few minor changes include canned corn, 2 cans of beans, salsa verde instead of tomatillos, and some thickening with 3 tablespoons of cornstarch in 1/2 c milk, all were suggestions from other reviews. I also simmered it for an hour. It is a nice change from the slow cooker taco soup that is also wonderful!

I am adding this last sentence after reading a more recent review by someone else who added lime to the chili and felt that it made it bitter....if you read the recipe again you will see that they suggest lime slices as a garnish:)

Delicious! I made this using a Costco rotisserie chicken, one cup of Del Real fresh green salsa and used frozen sweet corn. After sautéing the onions and garlic, I added the green chilis and tomatoes and used an immersion blender to puree (my kids don't like tomato and onion chunks). I then added the salsa, beans, chicken and corn. Very thick and plenty of heat! Garnished with fresh cilantro and sour cream. Made "Grandmother’s Buttermilk Cornbread Muffins" from this site. Great combination of flavors!

Absolutely delicious! I read quite a few reviews and used their advice. I did use rotisserie chicken, which gave it added flavor from the spices. I used 2 cans of white beans, as I wanted more beans. I put this on low in the crockpot for 6 hours. I used more broth, hoping I would have leftovers. Not the case. Everyone went back for seconds. I served it with sides of shredded cheese, sour cream, avocado and cilantro. Crusty bread was a nice compliment as well. Thank you for a great recipe!

This is a traditional recipe that I make for potlucks, I cook it in my InstaPot and cuts the time to make down to 20 mintues. The longer it sits in the refrigerator after the first day u eat it the better it is. The flavor's marry together, it's sooo delicious! When it's done cooking before serving I squeeze a lime, to taste into my bowl then I add a few black olives and a sprinkling of cilantro and a handful of chips. I put the montrey jack cheese and cheddar into the soup when its done cooking the, Enjoy and Bon Apetite!

Like most others here, I deviated from the recipe quite a bit, and the result was pretty tasty. I cooked my own beans (I used small red beans, but I think this would be fine with most kinds of beans), using about 1/2 lb. I used some fresh tomatillos (peeled, rinsed, blanched for 5 minutes, and chopped). The seasoning seemed far too little to get any decent flavor, so I used way more cumin and more oregano. I wasn't sure about the ground coriander (didn't know if I'd end up with something more like curry than chili), but I used some, and it tasted OK.

The recipe leaves out some important details, like what to do with the corn! I think it would be bad to just throw two whole ears of corn in, so I cut the kernels off (I used three ears) and then scraped the cobs to get all the starchy corn juice. This might have helped with thickening--it didn't seem too thin. 

I think this would be fine with more beans and less meat. Oh, and if you use canned beans, you might want to drain them and maybe rinse them.

One of the strangest things I saw in lots of reviews was that this was too spicy, which seems strange, since there is nothing spicy in the recipe at all. If you use something that's not in the recipe (e.g., salsa verde) and then find that the result is too spicy, you don't get to complain that it's the recipe's fault!

I followed the recipe. I didn't use canned Tom at ill's and roasted my own. It turns out that broiling and pureed the tomatillos made a natural thickener for the soup base. Can't wait for fresh green chili's. Absolutely tasty!

Day 2: This is delicious!! A late tasting resulted in an upgrade in the ranking. I almost couldn't stop eating it later in the day after the spices and flavors blended together. All I could think about was a taco party or a tailgate party with this as a mainstay on the taco bar. Definitely entering this recipe as one of my "best quick recipes of the year!! Day 1: I cut this recipe in half since I was only cooking for my self. You will have to adjust the seasonings depending on how much you are making. I've been looking for the white chicken chili recipe that I made over a year ago. I've tried several different ones from Allrecipes. I like a little creaminess to my white chicken chili so I added 1//2 cup plain greek yogurt to the recipe. I didn't have tomatillos but used green chilis instead. I think cream cheese would also work but I only had the yogurt. Also upped the spices for additional depth. Delicious on Day 1, can't wait to taste on Day 2.

I made the green salsa, 1 lb of tomatillos, 5 cloves of garlic, roasted in oven, 1/4 c of cilantro, 1/4 c of diced onion, 1 tsp cumin, 1/2 tsp salt. - need to simmer longer than recipe, may try 1 hr next time, might try 2nd can of beans. Did use 2 TBS of corn starch to thicken. Did add jalapeno.

My family loved this! I did add a can of black beans and 1/2 can hot rotelle tomatoes. It gave it a slight kick. I also used canned corn. Didn’t notice a difference. I Put in crock pot for two hours on high and two hours on low. Really helped blend the flavors. And it was so good!!!

It was super easy and delicious! I modified the recipe just tad and used my instant pot. I used about a pound of dried beans, 48 oz of chicken broth, and added about 2 cups of corn. I couldn’t find canned green chilies but used canned tomatoes with green chilies. I wish I had a used more tomatoes though. It cooked for 45 minutes and was done! Loved it

Because of lacking a few ingredients, I omitted the corn, tomatillo and jack cheese. Instead added a yellow bell pepper, a fresh tomato instead of can, 2 cans navy beans instead of one and melted in 1/4 cup cream cheese at the end. Fabulous!
Love to try something new
Easy instructions and substitute suggestions.

Loved this! My can of tomatillos was only 10 oz so I added a can of rotel tomato’s with chili. I also added an extra can of drained and rinsed white beans and smashed them up before adding. I didn’t have fresh corn so I used some frozen. I topped it with sour cream and cilantro. Very good!!

This was my first try at Chicken chili. It was easy to make and the flavor was great. I added 2 cans of beans and a can of tomatoes with green chili rain them along with the regular tomatoes, perfect amount of heat. I also roasted the tomato mood and blended them. It was a crowd pleaser for sure.
I fix this every Christmas Eve!! My family loves this! The only changes I made was canned corn and along with diced tomatoes I add a can of Rot Tel
Awesome!

Really good did a few things different to what i felt we would like, like a lil milk and corn starch to thicken up a lil, added a lil chicken bullion to give it a lil more savoury and knock down some of the tomatilla twang, used a queso white shreeded cheese, and a lil bit more oregano as well. About half the amout of green chillies cause the Misses cant handle the spicy so much. She absolutely loves it. I loved it was really good had to stop myself from over eating.🤣😂
I love this recipe. I used to make it at work when I cooked for 100 residents. I changed it up a bit by adding a little milk to make it creamier
